To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development of cytotoxic cells in response to syngeneictumor inoculation is modulated by memory and suppressor cells.
the cytotoxic response of tumor-primed spleen cells is mediated by at least three distinct subpopulations of cells: (a) memory cells, (b) effector cells, and (c) suppressor cells.
the development of a cytotoxic response to a syngenetic mammary adenocarcioma is a dynamic process involving the generation of at least four distinct populations of lymphoid cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of the development of cell-mediated immunity to a syngenic mammary adenocarcioma.
the kinetics of the immune response to syngeneically transplanted rat mammary adenocarcioma.
the development of memory and suppressive functions modulating the cellular cytotoxic response to a syngenetic mammary adenocarinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytolytic activity against syngeneic tumors is mediated by at least two populations of cells, cytolytic and suppressor.
a cytolytic response is a function of a series of interlocking events involving the interaction of at least three cell types: the effector cell, the memory cell, and a suppressor cell.

a single population of lymphoid cells is responsible for the generation of memory, cytotoxic and suppressor cells in the response of syngeneic rat spleen cells to syngeneically inoculated tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of a cytotoxic response is controlled by the interaction of at least three populations of lymphoid cells.
